questions.stem: All ganglia and sensory receptors are part of the _________; all the __________ are part of the CNS.
questions.answerRationale: His text: the PNS is the nerves, ganglia and sensory receptors; the CNS is the brain and spinal cord, so all the ventricles (cavities of the brain) are CNS.

questions.stem: Of the three meninges, ______________ is the innermost, and the three meninges cover _____________.

questions.stem: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) circulates in all these spaces EXCEPT ___________.

options.text: the central canal of the spinal cord
between the pia mater and arachnoid mater
between the arachnoid mater and dura mater

questions.answerRationale: His text: CSF circulates between the pia and arachnoid mater, in the ventricles and in the central canal; not between the arachnoid and dura.

questions.stem: The blood-brain barrier is created mainly by the _________, and _________ mater is the outermost of the three meninges of the brain.

options.text: tight junction of the capillary endothelial cells/ arachnoid
tightness of the basement membrane under the capillary endothelial cells/ pia

questions.answerRationale: His text says astrocytes cover the brain capillaries and form the blood-brain barrier; the dura is the outermost meninx. B and C pair a right first half with a wrong outermost layer.

questions.stem: Which of these parasites are paired with the disease they cause CORRECTLY?
questions.answerRationale: None of the four matches his text exactly: he lists Toxocara canis as causing ENCEPHALOPATHY, T. solium (not T. saginata) for cysticercosis, T. brucei for sleeping sickness, Naegleria for brain-eating disease. D (a Toxocara brain infection) is the only one not plainly wrong. Check this one if it appears.

questions.stem: Which of these statements about African Sleeping Sickness is CORRECT?

options.text: The causative agent is transmitted to humans by mosquitoes.
The infected subject develops nighttime insomnia but a daytime urge to sleep.
Urban citizens living in dense apartments are more vulnerable to getting the disease.
The disease is treated primarily with melarsoprol, a highly toxic arsenic organic compound.

questions.answerRationale: His text: stage 2 brings "daytime sleepiness, nighttime insomnia." Tsetse flies (not mosquitoes), rural (not urban), and melarsoprol "is no longer used."

questions.stem: One may develop brain cysticercosis if one ____________ and the disease is treated with ___________.

options.text: food contaminated with pig feces/ praziquantel
bitten by wild pig/ meglumine antimonate

questions.answerRationale: His text: eggs in SOILED food and drink, "not from consuming uncooked or undercooked pork," treated with albendazole or praziquantel. Only A has soiled food and a correct drug.

questions.stem: Which of these gives the most effective protection in preventing Acanthamoeba sp. infection of the eye?

options.text: Not using contact lenses while swimming in natural freshwater ponds.
Washing contact lenses daily with the prescribed cleaning solution.
Not using contact lenses (use prescription eyeglasses instead).

questions.answerRationale: His text: Acanthamoeba survives in contact lens cleaning solutions, so washing lenses (B) does not protect; contact lenses contaminated during swimming are the route. Not wearing lenses at all is the surest protection; A is the runner-up.

questions.stem: Which of these signs causes cerebral malaria and the related deaths?

options.text: The parasite destroys the liver, and liver failure causes encephalopathy
The parasite destroys red blood cells, and the cellular debris causes a brain stroke.
The parasite reproduces inside erythrocytes and alters its shape; the cells stick to the blood vessels in the brain.

questions.answerRationale: Not starred; answer derived from his Chapter 14 text.

questions.stem: Which of these statements is CORRECT about rabies?

options.text: Negri bodies found in the brain are inclusion particles made mainly of clumped rabies virus particles.
To be protected, one must receive the rabies vaccine before being bitten by a rabid animal.
Hydrophobia occurs because of schizophrenia-like behavioral changes in rabies patients.
Rabies cannot be transmitted from inhaled aerosols released by rabid animals.
The virus moves to the brain from the bite site via the blood.

questions.answerRationale: Negri bodies are clumps of rabies virus particles in brain cells. Pre-exposure vaccine is not required (post-exposure works), the virus travels to the brain along nerves, and bat-cave aerosols can transmit it.

questions.stem: The botulinum toxin (A subunit) causes flaccid paralysis by which of these mechanisms?

options.text: It cleaves snare proteins, thereby preventing the release of excitatory neurotransmitters.
It cleaves synaptobrevin proteins and thus prevents the release of inhibitory neurotransmitters.
It outcompetes excitatory neurotransmitters from binding to their receptors on the muscle cells.
It binds excitatory neurotransmitters and prevents the neurotransmitters from binding to their receptors.

questions.answerRationale: Not starred; answer derived from his Chapter 14 text.

questions.stem: Which of these pieces of information is CORRECT about Guillain-Barré syndrome? Note- Be specific.

options.text: It is caused by Zika virus, SARS-CoV-2, influenza, or Campylobacter jejuni.
It is treated with blood transfusion or temporary use of immunosuppressive drugs.
It is an autoimmune disease resulting from antibody-mediated destruction of neurons.
It occurs after infection with the influenza virus or Borrelia burgdorferi and is generally fatal.

questions.answerRationale: "Be specific": his text says antibodies made during infection bind neurons and destroy them through complement. A lists triggers, not the disease itself; treatment is plasmapheresis, not transfusion.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT an initial contributing factor to meningitis or an immediate outcome of meningitis?

options.text: Microbial PAMPs activating leucocytes in meninges.
Leukocyte migration and release of reactive oxygen species.
Intracranial pressure, brain swelling (edema), and damage to brain tissue.
Cytokine secretion, cytotoxic activities (cleaning infected cells), antibody deposition, and complement activation.

questions.answerRationale: Not starred; answer derived from his Chapter 14 text.

questions.stem: PCR using DNA extracted from the CSF of a person indicated the presence of the JC virus. Which of these statements is CORRECT about the patient?

options.text: The person was infected with the JC virus long ago.
The person may have a neurodegenerative disease
The person has an autoimmune brain destruction.
The person has a poor immune system.

questions.answerRationale: His text: almost everyone carries JC virus latently, and it reactivates only with severe immunosuppression, causing PML. A, B and D are all true, but C (autoimmune) is false, so "all these" fails; D is the specific clinical point. Runner-up E.

questions.stem: Which of these persons may develop spastic paralysis due to the tetanospasmin toxin of Clostridium tetani? Note: assume that none of these persons had a tetanus shot in the past ten years.

options.text: The person had received an injection to treat skin wrinkles from a physician’s assistant.
The person (adult) has eaten meat containing endospores of Clostridium tetani?

The person has stepped on a nail and has a deep wound.

questions.stem: Which of these statements is CORRECT about Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis (SSPE)?

options.text: The affected children have impaired cell-mediated immunity but produce antibodies against viral antigens.
The disease is caused by the measles vaccine because the vaccine is a live attenuated virus.
The disease signs appear within 6-10 months of initial measles infection.
The disease is caused by certain aggressive strains of the measles virus.

questions.answerRationale: His text: affected children show poor cell-mediated immunity but an excessive antibody response. Symptoms appear 6 to 10 YEARS later, the vaccine does not cause it, and the virus is a defective mutant, not an aggressive strain.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about diarrhea is INCORRECT?

options.text: The initial main concern of diarrhea is electrolyte and water loss.
It is defined as passing watery stool more than three times in 24 hours.
Untreated diarrhea may cause hypotension, organ failure, coma, and death
Injectable saline can be prepared by mixing 1 spoonful of NaCl, 1 spoonful of sucrose, and 2 liters of boiled water.
Viral diarrhea is generally acute and non-bleeding; bacterial diarrhea could be due to exotoxins and may involve blood loss.

questions.answerRationale: Salt, sugar and boiled water make an ORAL rehydration solution, not an injectable saline.

questions.stem: Why is antibiotic treatment insufficient in treating diphtheria, and must antiserum therapy be administered?

options.text: Corynebacterium diphtheriae is resistant to most antibiotics.
Antibiotics that kill the causative agent are too toxic to children.
The disease is caused by an exotoxin that the bacterium releases, not by the bacterium itself.
Only antiserum therapy may remove the diphtheria membrane from the mouth of the affected children.

questions.answerRationale: Not starred; answer derived from his Chapter 14 text.

questions.stem: Which of these ultimately causes cancer due to infection by Helicobacter pylori?

options.text: H. pylori survives in the intestine by creating ammonia from urea.
H pylori toxins cause dysplasia and metaplasia of the stomach epithelial cells.
Activated leucocytes migrate into the inflamed stomach mucosa and release ROSs and NO.
The thick layers of mucus on the gastric epithelium deteriorate, exposing the mucosa to gastric acid.

questions.answerRationale: His text: leukocytes release ROS and NO that cause DNA damage in stomach cells, and some become tumors. Toxins contributing to metaplasia and dysplasia (B) are also in his text, so B is the runner-up.

questions.stem: Which of these causes liver fibrosis and hepatic hypertension? Note: Be specific.

options.text: Chronic inflammation, continuous killing, and regeneration of liver cells.
Death of hepatocytes and the reduced processing of bilirubin and other toxic chemicals.
Activated stellate cells of the liver differentiate into myofibroblasts and secrete collagen.
Increase in the size of the liver due to unregulated regrowth (regeneration) of the liver tissues.

questions.answerRationale: "Be specific": his text says activated stellate cells differentiate into myofibroblasts that lay down collagen.

questions.stem: Oxygen in the air of the alveoli must diffuse through each of these obstacles to reach the iron atoms of the hemoglobin inside the erythrocytes. Which of them is the first of the obstacles?

options.text: Basement membrane of the blood capillaries.
Endothelial cells of the blood capillaries.

questions.answerRationale: His text: oxygen diffuses through the surfactant fluid first, then the alveolar epithelium, basement membrane, endothelium and plasma.

questions.stem: A person breathes between 17,000 and 23,000 times in 24 hours, and inhales about 500 ml of air/breath. If one milliliter of air contains one dust particle or microbes (viruses, bacteria, fungal spores, protozoan cysts, or worm eggs), how many particles does the person inhale daily?
questions.answerRationale: 17,000 x 500 mL = 8.5 million; 23,000 x 500 mL = 11.5 million, so about 9 to 12 million.

questions.stem: Untreated bronchitis/bronchiolitis may develop chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and emphysema, especially among smokers. Which of these is strictly a specific sign of emphysema?
questions.answerRationale: His text: COPD becomes emphysema when it involves alveolar damage. Chest tightness, blockage and shortness of breath are COPD in general.

Infection/inflammation of the conjunctiva, cornea, and retina.
Keratoconjunctivitis caused by a particular bacterial species.
Keratoconjunctivitis caused by a particular viral species.
Infection/inflammation of the conjunctiva and cornea.

questions.stem: How is croup different from simple coughs?

options.text: Croup involves a hoarse cough; simple coughing does not.
Croup is a reflex to clear the airways by forced exhaling; cough is not.
Croup does not involve breathing and swallowing difficulties; coughing does.
Croup is usually due to bacterial infections, and simple coughing is usually due to viral infections.

questions.answerRationale: His text: croup is "marked by a barking (hoarse) cough."

questions.stem: Recovery from viral and bacterial lung infection may lead to lung fibrosis. Which of these describes lung fibrosis properly?

questions.stem: Which of this information about influenza is INCORRECT?

options.text: The causative agents are some of the most rapidly evolving pathogens known.
The disease signs may include ARDS, pneumonia, cardiovascular complications, and encephalitis.
The incidence and mortality due to the disease in the US are about 50 million and 40,000, respectively.
Annual vaccination, frequent handwashing, and using masks fully protect health care workers from infection.

questions.answerRationale: His text gives about 50 million cases and over 40,000 deaths (so C is correct) and says vaccinated people are "not completely protected." "Fully protect" is the incorrect statement.

questions.stem: Which of these is a sign of acute otitis media?

options.text: Pain, swelling, and drainage from open wounds of the outer ears.
An otoscopic examination shows a reddened/ inflamed eardrum.
An otoscopic examination shows fluid and pus under the eardrum.
An otoscopic examination shows a perforated eardrum releasing pus.
The affected subject has vertigo after recovering from a systemic viral infection.

questions.answerRationale: His text describes middle-ear fluid, gas and pressure behind the eardrum (and rupture in severe cases); pus and fluid under the eardrum is the defining sign. A is otitis externa; E is labyrinthitis. Runner-up B.

questions.stem: Which of these is MDR-TB?

options.text: Active TB, the bacillus is resistant to isoniazid and rifampicin.
Asymptomatic TB, found among 95% of patients after initial infection by the bacillus.
In active TB, the bacillus is resistant to isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, or ethambutol.
Active TB, the bacillus is resistant to fluoroquinolone, and at least one of the three injectable second-line antibiotics.

questions.answerRationale: MDR-TB means resistant to at least isoniazid and rifampicin (D describes XDR-TB).

questions.stem: Which of these statements about whopping cough is INCORRECT?

options.text: The disease is caused by multiple bacterial pathogens.
The disease is caused by an exotoxin, not by the bacteria.
Older children and the elderly in the United States are getting the disease.
The disease is named for the hoarse noise during the exhalation phase of the cough.
The disease can make children get exhausted and may cause seizures, brain damage, and death.

questions.answerRationale: His text: the loud whoop comes when the child struggles to INHALE after the paroxysm, not during exhalation.
